written.myAnswer: Vegetative propagation can produce many plants quickly, and the offspring retain the parent’s useful characteristics. A disadvantage is that the offspring have little genetic variation, so they may be similarly vulnerable to environmental changes, diseases, or pests.

Cutting: A piece of stem or root is cut from a plant and used to grow a new plant. Grafting: A bud or small stem of one plant is attached to the root or stem of another plant; this can combine beneficial characteristics of the two plants.

Vegetative propagation is the production of new plants from vegetative parts, such as stems, roots, or leaves. Artificial propagation is the production of new plants by human-directed methods, such as cutting, grafting, and tissue culture.

Humans can grow new plants using cutting, grafting, or tissue culture. In cutting, a piece of stem or root is used to grow a new plant. In grafting, a bud or small stem of one plant is attached to the root or stem of another, which can combine beneficial characteristics. Tissue culture grows plants from cells or tissues under controlled conditions.

Asexual reproduction generally produces offspring genetically like the parent and does not create much genetic variation. Sexual reproduction combines genetic material from gametes and can produce variation among offspring.
